verses.eng: against you, to take from you your light, in order that he may send it down into the chaos and it may get down to that emanation of his, so that it may be able to come up out of the chaos and go to his region. Adamas will attempt this. But I will take all your powers from him and give them to you, and I will come to take them. Now, therefore, if they constrain you at that time, then sing praises to the Light, and I will not delay to help you. And I will quickly come to you to the regions which are below you. And I will come down to their regions to take their light from them. And I will come to this region where I have removed you, and which is below the thirteenth aeon, until I bring you to your region from where you are come.'

"It came to pass then, when Pistis Sophia had heard me say these words to her, that she rejoiced with great joy. But I removed her to the region which is below the thirteenth aeon. I went to the Light and departed from her."

And all these adventures the First Mystery told to the disciples, that they should come to pass for Pistis Sophia. And he sat on the Mount The time for the final deliverance of Sophia is completed. of Olives, narrating all these adventures in the midst of the disciples. And he continued again and said to them: "And it came to pass again after this, while I was in the world of men and sat in the way, that is in this region which is the Mount of Olives, before my vesture was sent to me, which I had deposited in the four-and-twentieth mystery from the interior, but the first from the exterior, which is the Great Uncontainable, in which I am enwrapped, and before I had gone to the Height to receive my second vesture,--
while I sat with you in this region, which is the Mount of Olives, that the time was completed of which I had said to Pistis Sophia: 'Adamas and all his rulers will constrain you.'

"It came to pass then, when that time came on,--and I was in the world of men, sitting with you in this region, which is the Mount of Olives,--that Adamas looked down out of the twelve aeons and looked down at the regions of the chaos and saw his demon power which is in the chaos, that no light at all was in it, because I had taken its light from it; and he saw it, that it was dark and Adamas sends forth two emanations of darkness to plague Sophia. could not go to his region, that is to the twelve moons. Thereon Adamas again remembered Pistis Sophia and became most exceedingly wroth against her, thinking that it was she who had imprisoned his power in the chaos, and thinking that it was she who had taken its light from it. And he was exceedingly embittered; he piled wrath on wrath and emanated out of himself a dark emanation and another, chaotic and evil, the violent one], so as through them to harass Pistis Sophia. And he made a dark region in his region, so as to constrain Sophia therein. And he took many of his rulers; they pursued after Sophia, in order that the two dark emanations which Adamas had emanated, might lead her into the dark chaos which he had made, and constrain her in that region and harass her, until they should take her whole light from her, and Adamas should take the light from Pistis Sophia and give it to the two dark violent emanations, and they should carry it to the great chaos which is below and dark, and cast it into his dark power which is chaotic, if perchance it might be able to come to his
region, because it had become exceedingly dark, for I had taken its light-power from it.

Sophia again sings a song to the Light. "'1. O Light of lights, I have had faith in you. Save me from all these rulers who pursue after me, and help me, "'2. That in sooth they may never take from me my light, as the lion-faced power did]. For your light is not with me and your light-stream to save me. Nay, Adamas is the more enraged against me, saying to me: You have imprisoned my power in the chaos. "'3. Now, therefore, O Light of lights, if I have done this and have imprisoned it, if I have done any injustice at all to that power, "'4. Or if I have constrained it, as it has constrained me, then let all these rulers who pursue after me, take my light from me and leave me empty; "'5. And let foe Adamas pursue after my power and seize upon it and take my light from me and cast it into his dark power which is in the chaos, and keep my power in the chaos. "'6. Now, therefore, O Light, lay hold on me in your wrath and lift up your power above my foes who have lifted themselves up against me to the very end. "'7. Quicken me quickly, as you have said to me: I will help you.'

It came to pass then, when the First Mystery had finished saying these words to the disciples, that he said: "Who has understood the words which I have spoken, let him come forward and set forth their solution."
Yaiqab came forward and said: "My Adanay, concerning this song which Pistis Sophia has sung, thus your light-power has prophesied aforetime through Dawad in the seventh Psalm:

Yaiqab interprets the song from Psalm vii. "'1. O Adanay, my God, in you have I hoped. Free me from my pursuers and save me, "'2. That in sooth he may never steal away my soul as an lion, without any one to deliver and save. "'3. O Adanay, my God, if I have done this, if injustice is on my hands, "'4. If I have requited those who requite me with evil, then let me fall down empty through my foes. "'5. And let the foe pursue after my soul and seize it, and trample my life to the ground and lay my honour in the dustSelah. "'6. Arise, O Adanay, in your wrath, raise yourself up for the end of my foes. "'7. Arise according to the commandment which you have commanded.'" It came to pass then, when the First Mystery had heard Yaiqab speak these words, that he said: Well said, Yaiqab, beloved."
And the First Mystery continued again and said to the disciples: "It came to pass then, when Pistis Sophia had finished uttering the words of this song, that she turned herself back
to see whether Adamas and his rulers had turned back to go to their aeon. And she saw them, how they pursued after her. Then she turned to them and said to them:

Sophia addresses Adamas and his rulers. "'1. Dan pursue you after me and say: I should not have help, that it [ sc. the Light] should save me from you? "'2. Now, therefore, my vindicator is the Light and a strong one]; but it is long-suffering until the time of which it has said to me: I will come and help you. And it will not bring its wrath upon you always. But this is the time of which he has spoken to me. "'3. Now, therefore, if you turn not back and cease not to pursue after me, then will the Light make ready its power, and it will make itself ready in all its powers. "'4. And in its power has it made itself ready, so that it may take your lights which are in you, and you may become dark; and its power has brought it to pass, so that it may take your power from you and you go to ground.'

"And when Pistis Sophia had said this, she looked at the region of Adamas and saw the dark and chaotic region which he had made, and saw also the two dark exceedingly violent emanations which Adamas had emanated, in order that they might seize Pistis Sophia and cast her down into the chaos which he had made, and constrain and harass her in that region, until they should take her light from her. It came to pass then, when Pistis Sophia had seen those two dark emanations and the dark region which Adamas had made, that she feared and cried to the Light, saying:

Sophia again sings to the Light. "'1. O Light, lo! Adamas, the doer of violence, is wrathful; he has made a dark emanation, "'2. And he has also emanated another chaos and has made another dark and chaotic one] and made it ready. "'3. Now, therefore, O Light, the chaos which he has made, in order to cast me down therein and take from me my light-power, take then from him his own. "'4. And the plan which he has devised, to take my light,--they are to take his own from him; and the injustice which he has spoken, to take my lights from me,--take then all of his.'

"These are the words which Pistis Sophia has uttered in her song. Now, therefore, who is sober in spirit, let him come forward and set forth the solution of the words which Pistis Sophia [has uttered] in her song."
Marathaa again came forward and said: "My Adanay, I am sober in my spirit and understand the words which you say. Now, therefore, give me commandment to set forth their solution in openness."
And the First Mystery answered and said to Marathaa: "I give you commandment, Marathaa, to set forth the solution of the words which Pistis Sophia has uttered in her song."

And Marathaa answered and said: "My Adanay, these are the words which your light-power has prophesied aforetime through Dawad in the seventh Psalm, saying: "'12. God is a righteous vindicator and strong and long-suffering, who brings not on his wrath every day.

Marathaa interprets the words of Sophia from Psalm vii. "'13. If you turn not, he will whet his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready. "'14. And he has made ready for him instruments of death; he has made his arrows for those who will be burnt up. "'15. Behold, injustice has been in labour, has conceived wrong and brought forth iniquity. "'16. It has digged a pit and hollowed it out. It will fall into the hole which it has made. "'17. Its wrong will return on its own head, and its injustice will come down on its pate.'"
When Marathaa had said this, the First Mystery which looks without, said to her: Well said, finely, Marathaa, blessed one]."

Jesus brings Sophia again to the thirteenth aeon. It came to pass then, when Jesus had finished telling his disciples all the adventures which had befallen Pistis Sophia when she was in the chaos, and the way she had sung praises to the Light, that it should save her and lead her out of the chaos, and lead her into the twelve aeons, and also the way it had saved her out of all her afflictions with which the rulers of the chaos had constrained her, because she longed to go to the Light, that Jesus continued again in the discourse and said to his disciples: "It came to pass then after all this, that I took Pistis Sophia and led her into the thirteenth aeon, shining most exceedingly, there being no measure for the light which was about me. I entered into the region of the four-and-twenty invisibles, shining most exceedingly. And they fell into great commotion; they looked and saw Sophia, who was with me. Her they knew, but me they knew not, who I was, but held me for some sort of emanation of the Light-land.

"It came to pass then, when Pistis Sophia saw her fellows, the invisibles, that she rejoiced in great joy and exulted exceedingly and desired to proclaim the wonders which I had wrought on her below in the earth of mankind, until I saved her. She came into the midst of the invisibles, and in their midst sang praises to me, saying:

Sophia sings the praises of the Light to her fellow-invisibles. "'1. I will give thanks to you, O Light, for you are a saviour; you are a deliverer for all time. "'2. I will utter this song to the Light, for it has saved me and saved me out of the hand of the rulers, my foes. "'3. And you have preserved me in all the regions, you have saved me out of the height and the depth of the chaos and out of the aeons of the rulers of the sphere. "'4. And when I was come out of the Height, I wandered round in regions in which is no light, and I could not return to the thirteenth aeon, my dwelling-place. "'5. For there was no light in me nor power. My power was utterly ?. "'6. And the Light saved me in all my afflictions. I sang praises to the Light, and it hearkened to me, when I was constrained. "'7. It guided me in the creation of the aeons to lead me up into the thirteenth aeon, my dwelling-place. "'8. I will give thanks to you, O Light, that you have saved me, and for your wondrous works to the race of men. "'9. When I failed of my power, you have given me power; and when I failed of my light, you did fill me with purified light. "'10. I was in the darkness and in the shadow of the chaos, bound with the mighty fetters of the chaos, and no light was in me. "'11. For I have provoked the commandment of the Light and have transgressed, and I have made wroth the commandment of the Light, because I had gone out of my region. "'12. And when I had gone down, I failed of my light and became without light, and no one had helped me. "'13. And in my affliction I sang praises to the Light, and it saved me out of my afflictions. "'14. And it has also broken asunder all my bonds and led me up out of the darkness and the affliction of the chaos. "'15. I will give thanks to you, O Light, that you have saved me and that your wondrous works have been wrought in the race of men. "'16. And you have shattered the upper gates of the darkness and the mighty bolts of the chaos. "'17. And you did let me depart out of the region in which I had transgressed, and my light was taken, because I have transgressed. "'18. And I ceased from my mysteries and went down to the gates of the chaos. "'19. And when I was constrained, I sang praises to the Light. It saved me out of all my afflictions. "'20. You sent your stream; it gave me power and saved me out of all my afflictions. "'21. I will give thanks to you, O Light, that you have saved me, and for your wondrous works in the race of men.'
"This then is the song which Pistis Sophia

has uttered in the midst of the four-and-twenty invisibles, desiring that they should know all the wondrous works which I had done for her, and desiring that they should know that I have gone to the world of men and have given them the mysteries of the Height. Now, therefore, who is exalted in his thought, let him come forward and say the solution of the song which Pistis Sophia has uttered."

It came to pass then, when Jesus had finished saying these words, that Payalayapawas came forward and said: Jesus, my Adanay, my thought is exalted, and I have understood the solution of the song which Pistis Sophia has uttered. The prophet Dawad has prophesied concerning it aforetime in the sixth Psalm, saying:

Payalayapawas interprets the song from Psalm cvi. "'1. Give you thanks to the Adanay, for he is good, for his grace is eternal. "'2. Let the delivered of the Adanay say this, for it is he who has delivered them out of the hand of their foes. "'3. He has gathered them together out of their lands, from the east and from the west and from the north and from the sea. "'4. They wandered round in the desert, in a waterless country; they found not the way to the city of their dwelling-place. "'5. Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them. "'6. He saved them out of their necessities. They cried to the Adanay and he hearkened to them in their affliction. "'7. He led them on a straight way, that they might go to the region of their dwelling-place. "'8. Let them give thanks to the Adanay for

his graciousness and his wondrous works to the children of men. "'9. For he has satisfied a hungering soul; he has filled a hungering soul with good things, "'10. Them who sat in darkness and the shadow of death, who were fettered in misery and iron. "'11. For they had provoked the word of God and made wroth the determination of the Ilayawan. "'12. Their heart was humbled in their miseries; they become weak and no one helped them. "'13. They cried to the Adanay in their affliction; he saved them out of their necessities. "'14. And he led them out of the darkness and the shadow of death and broke their bonds asunder. "'15. Let them give thanks to the Adanay for his graciousness and his wondrous works to the children of men. "'16. For he has shattered the gates of brass and burst the bolts of iron asunder. "'17. He has taken them to himself out of the way of their iniquity. For they were brought low because of their iniquities. "'18. Their heart abhorred all manner of meat and they were near to the gates of death. "'19. They cried to the Adanay in their affliction and he saved them out of their necessities. "'20. He sent his word and healed them and freed them from their miseries. "'21. Let them give thanks to the Adanay for
his graciousness and his wondrous works to the children of men.'

"This then, my Adanay, is the solution of the song which Pistis Sophia has uttered. Hearken, therefore, my Adanay, that I may say it clearly. The word in Booth which Dawad has spoken: Give you thanks to the Adanay, for he is good, for his grace is eternal,'--it is the word which Pistis Sophia has spoken: 'I will give thanks to you, O Light, for you are a saviour and you are a deliverer for all time.'

"And the word which has Dawad spoken: 'Let the delivered of the Adanay say this, for he has delivered them out of the hand of their foes,'--it is the word which Pistis Sophia has spoken: 'I will utter this song to the Light, for it has saved me and saved me out of the hand of the rulers, my foes.' And the rest of the Psalm.

"This then, my Adanay, is the solution of the song which Pistis Sophia has uttered in the midst of the four-and-twenty invisibles, desiring that they should know all the wondrous works which you have done for her, and desiring that they should know that you have given your mysteries to the race of men."
It came to pass then, when Jesus had heard Payalayapawas say these words, that he said: Well said, blessed Payalayapawas. This is the solution of the song which Pistis Sophia has uttered."
Marayam questions Jesus. It came to pass then again, after all this, that Marayam came forward, adored the feet of Jesus and said: "My Adanay, be not wroth with me, if I

question you, because we question concerning everything with precision and certainty. For you have said to us aforetime: Seek that you may find, and knock that it may be opened to you. For every one who seeks shall find, and to every one who knocks it shall be opened.' Now, therefore, my Adanay, who is it whom I shall seek, or who is it at whom we shall knock? Or who rather is able to give us the decision upon the words concerning which we shall question you? Or who rather knows the power of the words concerning which we shall question? Because you in the mind have given us mind of the Light and have given us sense and a exceedingly exalted thought; for which cause, therefore, no one exists in the world of men nor any one in the height of the aeons, who can give the decision on the words concerning which we question, save you alone, who knows [ sic ] the universe, who is perfected in the universe; because we do not question in the manner in which the men of the world question, but because we question in the gnosis of the Height which you have given to us, and we question moreover in the type of the excellent questioning which you have taught us, that we may question therein. Now, therefore, my Adanay, be not wroth with me, but reveal to me the matter concerning which I shall question you."

It came to pass, when Jesus had heard Marayam Magdalene say these words, that he answered and said to her: "Question concerning what you desire to question, and I will reveal it to you with precision and certainty. Aman, amen, I say to you: Rejoice in great joy and exult

most exceedingly. If you question concerning all with precision, then shall I exult most exceedingly, because you question concerning all with precision and question in the manner in which it beseems to question. Now, therefore, question concerning what you would question, and I will reveal it to you with joy."

It came to pass then, when Marayam had heard the Saviour say these words, that she rejoiced in great joy and exulted most exceedingly and said to Jesus: "My Adanay and Saviour, of what manner then are the four-and-twenty invisibles and of what type, or rather of what quality are they, or of what quality is then their light?"

Of the glory of the four-and-twenty invisibles. And Jesus answered and said to Marayam: "What is there in this world which is like to them, or rather what region is there in this world which is comparable to them? Now, therefore, to what am I to liken them, or rather what am I to say concerning them? For nothing exists in this world to which I shall be able to liken them, and no form exists in it which is able to be like them. Now, therefore, nothing exists in this world which is of the quality of the heaven. [But] amen, I say to you: Every one of the invisibles is nine times greater than the heaven and the sphere above it and the twelve aeons all together, as I have already said to you at another time. And no light exists in this world which is more excellent than the light of the sun. Aman, amen, I say to you: The four-and-twenty invisibles shine thousand times more than the light of the sun which is in this world, as I have already said to you at another time. For the light
